campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16: tensor parallelism flips which side of a tie the sequential oracle takes (2026-09-09)
question: Sites have been shown stable across days, boots and compilation modes. Tensor parallelism is the one change that alters the arithmetic itself - the all-reduce introduces a different summation order. If these sites are ties, TP should not remove them; it should be able to move which side wins.
method: Compared the c64 depth-3 site sets of the TP1 arms (f1+f2 pooled, 40 passes, 340 events) and the TP2 arm (t1, 2 passes, 9 events). A site was first defined as (prompt_id, index, oracle token, run token) and then, when that made the sets look disjoint, as (prompt_id, index, unordered token pair) with the direction reported separately.
the_ordered_definition_is_misleading_her: By the ordered definition, 0 of 7 TP2 sites match any of the 19 TP1 sites. That reads as two unrelated fragile sets. It is an artifact: by the unordered definition 4 of the 7 match, and every one of the four is direction-reversed.

sites.tp1: oracle emits ' resource', concurrent runs emit ' constraint' (36 events)
sites.tp2: oracle emits ' constraint', concurrent runs emit ' resource' (2 events)

sites.tp1: oracle emits ' hang', concurrent runs emit ' leave' (17 events)
sites.tp2: oracle emits ' leave', concurrent runs emit ' hang' (2 events)

sites.tp1: oracle emits ' "', concurrent runs emit ' update' (8 events)
sites.tp2: oracle emits ' update', concurrent runs emit ' "' (1 event)

sites.tp1: oracle emits ' data', concurrent runs emit ' historical' (6 events)
sites.tp2: oracle emits ' historical', concurrent runs emit ' data' (1 event)

reading: At each of these four positions the model is choosing between two continuations and four different execution conditions distribute over the two candidates: single-stream TP1 takes side A, concurrent TP1 takes side B, single-stream TP2 takes side B, and concurrent TP2 takes side A. TP1's concurrent answer is TP2's sequential answer at every one of the four. The site is a property of the model and the prompt; which side wins is set by the arithmetic, and a change as ordinary as adding a second card is enough to move it.

the_branches_are_whole_continuations.test: If a site is a binary fork between two coherent continuations, then a TP1 concurrent response that flipped the fork should not merely differ at that one token - it should be the entire TP2 sequential response.
the_branches_are_whole_continuations.result: It is, exactly, in three of the four sites: capacity-c062, rollback-c010 and cache-c016 each have a TP1 concurrent response byte-identical to the TP2 sequential oracle across all 128 tokens, while the TP1 and TP2 oracles themselves diverge at the site index (54, 112 and 26 respectively).
the_branches_are_whole_continuations.the_fourth: capacity-c022 agrees with the TP2 oracle for 17 tokens and then parts. That prompt carries a second, independent site at index 93, so the two responses take the same branch at the first fork and different branches at the second. Consistent with the model rather than an exception to it.
the_branches_are_whole_continuations.why_it_matters: This is the strongest form of the claim available from output alone. A site is not a corrupted token; it is a fork between two complete, deterministic continuations, and every execution condition lands cleanly on one branch or the other. Flipping the fork by any means - concurrency, a second card - returns the other branch in full.

reverse_direction.test: The mirror of the first test: does a TP2 concurrent response that flipped the fork equal the TP1 sequential oracle?
reverse_direction.result: For the two prompts that carry a single site it is exact in both directions. capacity-c062 and rollback-c010 each give TP1-concurrent byte-identical to TP2-sequential and TP2-concurrent byte-identical to TP1-sequential, all 128 tokens.
reverse_direction.the_two_prompts_with_a_second_site: cache-c016 agrees with the TP1 oracle for 50 tokens and capacity-c022 for 93, and those are exactly where each carries its second site (cache-c016 has sites at 26 and 50; capacity-c022 at 17 and 93). They take the same branch at the first fork and different branches at the second, which is what a multi-fork model predicts rather than an exception to it.
reverse_direction.the_full_picture: For a single-site prompt there are exactly two continuations and the four execution conditions map onto them as a clean 2x2: TP1 sequential and TP2 concurrent give branch A; TP1 concurrent and TP2 sequential give branch B. Nothing produces a third continuation, and nothing produces a partially corrupted one.

how_to_say_this_publicly: A divergence at one of these sites is not a wrong answer. Both branches are fluent, both are correct, and the model is choosing between synonyms at a point where its own logits do not separate them. 'Lossless' on this lane means the strict gates pass, not that the model has a single determined output at every position - it does not, and no kernel change can give it one.

strength_and_limits.statistics: 4 of 4 reversed is p = 1/16 = 0.0625 against a null in which direction is set at random per site per configuration. On its own that is suggestive, not conclusive.
strength_and_limits.why_it_is_still_strong: It is not an isolated observation. It agrees with the 39 bidirectional sites found across the 27B, 9B and 4B lanes, with cache-c016 and cache-c056 resolving the same pair oppositely inside one campaign, with the decoded pairs being synonyms in every case, and with the FP8 build showing exactly two variants per tie-prone prompt at concurrency 1. Five independent lines, one model.
strength_and_limits.sample_size: The TP2 arm is 2 passes and 9 events. Its three non-shared sites are the low-rate tail that two passes cannot separate from the shared set, not evidence of TP2-specific sites. Chain 3's t5 arm adds 20 TP2 passes at c64 and will settle that.
strength_and_limits.not_claimed: This does not say TP2 is better or worse. Both configurations diverge under concurrency; they simply disagree about which side of these ties is the sequential answer.

consequence_for_the_lane: An oracle is bound to an arithmetic, which AGENTS.md rule 2 already states for kernels. This extends it to topology: a TP1 oracle is not a valid reference for a TP2 candidate at these sites, and a cross-topology exactness comparison would report divergence that is entirely the oracle's side of the tie changing. Every campaign on this lane already regenerates its oracle per configuration, so nothing measured is affected - but the rule is worth stating explicitly for topology, not only for kernels.
